headline: Williams Jr. fuels Washington past Michigan State 25-18
dek: Washington opens 1-0 atop the power poll while Michigan State drops to 0-1 and last in the Western Central.
body: Fourth quarter, 2:44 remaining, Washington ball at its own 37, second-and-4, clinging to a 25-18 lead. Demond Williams Jr. hands to Jordan Washington for three yards, then five on third-and-short, then Bonner Jr. rips off ten and four more to grind out first downs and bleed the clock. The Huskies kneel it out at the Michigan State 45 with 47 seconds left, sealing a 25-18 win.

Washington struck first, capping a 10-play, 80-yard opening drive with Bonner Jr.'s short touchdown run and a successful two-point try at 1:54 of the first quarter for an 8-0 edge. A 44-yard strike to Kade Eldridge set up a nine-yard touchdown catch by Justice Williams at 12:07 of the second, and a Glass fumble recovered by Rahshawn Clark at the Michigan State 30 led to a 38-yard Luke Dunne field goal and an 18-0 Washington lead at 8:07. Michigan State answered with a 78-yard drive finished by Arnold Glass finding George Sater from seven yards at 2:00, then a 41-yard Keith Rocha field goal at 4:43 of the third cut it to 18-10. Williams Jr. hit Eldridge for a one-yard score on the first play of the fourth to make it 25-10, and Glass connected with Jason Walsh on a four-yard touchdown with a two-point conversion at 10:54 to pull within seven, but the Huskies' final drive iced it.

The box score tells the story: Washington outgained Michigan State 367-215, led by Williams Jr.'s 265 passing yards, two passing scores and 91 rushing yards with a touchdown — good for Player of the Game honors. The Huskies converted 55 percent of third downs to Michigan State's 43 percent, and the lone turnover that mattered was Glass's second-quarter fumble that set up Dunne's field goal; Michigan State's only takeaway came on a muffed punt return at 13:22 of the fourth but produced no points. Bonner Jr. added 91 rushing yards and a score on eight carries, while Justice Williams paced Washington receivers with five catches for 95 yards, placing him third in the PCFL in receiving yards after Week 1. For Michigan State, Glass threw for 144 yards and two touchdowns with a 104.6 rating, 12th in the league in passing yards, and Toi Bernard broke a 31-yard run, but the Spartans managed just 97 rushing yards and 14 first downs.

Washington moves to 1-0, jumps to No. 1 in the power poll and sits second in the Western Pacific behind division leader USC at 1-0. Michigan State falls to 0-1, drops to No. 10 in the poll and occupies the Western Central cellar while Notre Dame leads the division. Next week the Spartans travel to face USC (1-0), while Washington returns home to host Miami (0-1).
turningPoint: Glass's fumble at the Michigan State 30 with 9:05 left in the second quarter, recovered by Clark, set up Dunne's 38-yard field goal that pushed Washington's lead to 18-0.
byTheNumbers: Washington 367 total yards vs. Michigan State 215 — the Huskies' offense ranked 10th in the PCFL after Week 1 while the Spartans sat 17th.
Williams Jr. 265 passing yards, 91 rushing yards, three total touchdowns — the only player in Week 1 with 250+ passing and 90+ rushing.
Third-down conversion: Washington 55% (6/11), Michigan State 43% (6/14) — the Huskies sustained drives, the Spartans stalled.
Turnover margin: each team lost one fumble, but Washington turned its takeaway into three points; Michigan State's takeaway yielded zero.

unsungHero.name: Kade Eldridge
unsungHero.why: Caught a 44-yard reception that set up Washington's second touchdown and added the fourth-quarter one-yard scoring catch that made it a two-score game.
